passage: In the courtyard of their village house, Bhavna and her cousin Kunal shared her father's old phone. A bright box popped up over the game: "Golden skin, today only!" Bhavna's thumb hovered. Her character looked plain beside the others, and a win would look good too. "Everyone will laugh at the plain one," Kunal joked. She wanted it. She also knew the game wanted her to want it. "I'll ask Papa first," she said, and went to the shed where he was mending a wheel. Papa said not today. When she came back, Kunal shrugged. "I don't care what skin you have. I like playing with you."

qa.q: Who did Bhavna go to ask before buying the golden skin?
qa.a: She went to ask Papa in the shed.

qa.q: What was Bhavna feeling as her thumb hovered over the golden skin?
qa.a: She felt tempted but torn: she wanted to look good and win, yet she also sensed that the game was designed to make her want it.

qa.q: Why is asking a parent before spending a wise step for Bhavna?
qa.a: The game is built to tempt, and a parent can help her decide with a cooler head and an eye on what things really cost.

qa.q: How does Kunal see the skin?
qa.a: As no big deal: he joked about it at first, but then said he did not care what skin she has and just likes playing with her.

grounding: Illustrates a child pressed by in-game purchase offers who asks a parent first and learns a friend does not care about skins.

passage:
"Nilesh, look! The golden armour's on sale, only two hours left!"
"How much?"
"Ninety-nine rupees. Everyone in my team has it. I look like a beginner without it."
"Didn't you want a glowing sword last month too?"
"This is different. It says 'Buy now, don't miss out!'"
"It always says that."
Sarika frowned. "It does?"
"Every week. They put a timer so you panic."
"Oh." She watched the numbers ticking down. "Mummy's card is saved on the tablet. I could just tap."
"Then ask Mummy first."
Sarika carried the tablet to the balcony. Mummy listened and said, "Let's leave it today. If you still want it next week, we'll talk it over together."
Sarika sighed, then shrugged. "Pakhi never even looks at what I'm wearing anyway."

qa.q: How much time did the sale timer say was left?
Why did Sarika want the golden armour so badly?
qa.a: She felt left out and a little embarrassed, like a beginner, because her team already had it.

qa.q: What made Sarika slow down before spending?
qa.a: Nilesh pointed out that the timer comes back every week to make players panic, and she asked Mummy first.

qa.q: How does Nilesh see the sale timer?
qa.a: Nilesh sees it as a trick that returns every week to make players panic and tap.

grounding: A girl pressured by a game's timed offer to look cool pauses, asks a parent before spending, and remembers friends don't care about outfits.

passage:
I'm Jasleen. Last month a game I love started showing a shiny panda outfit every time I lost a level. "Win faster with Panda Power!" it flashed. After a few days I truly believed I couldn't win without it. I even counted my birthday money in my head.
Then I noticed something. The pop-up came right after I lost, every single time, when I felt worst. That wasn't luck; somebody planned it that way.
I asked Papa before buying anything, and he said to wait a week and see if I still wanted it. I also asked my friend Chetan if my plain outfit looked silly. He laughed. "I never even noticed what you wear. I just like racing you." I never bought the panda.

qa.q: When did the panda outfit pop-up appear?
qa.a: Right after Jasleen lost a level, every single time.

qa.q: What was Jasleen worried about before talking to Chetan?
qa.a: Jasleen was worried the plain outfit looked silly and felt unable to win without the panda.

qa.q: Which steps helped Jasleen resist the pressure?
qa.a: Noticing the pop-up was timed for the worst moments, asking Papa before buying, and checking with Chetan.

qa.q: How does Chetan see Jasleen's outfit?
qa.a: Chetan does not care about it at all; racing together is what matters.

grounding: A child notices a game's purchase offers are designed to tempt, asks a parent before spending and learns a real friend doesn't care about skins.
